A tyre manufacturer wants longer life. A shipowner wants less corrosion. A data-centre operator needs to remove more heat.

HydroGraph’s graphene could help all three.

Its application work targets expensive problems across industries:

🛞 TYRES — Reinforce rubber to improve wear resistance and durability. Longer-lasting tyres could lower replacement costs and waste.

🛡️ COATINGS — Slow the penetration of water and oxygen, helping protect ships, bridges and industrial equipment from corrosion.

🏗️ CONCRETE — Reduce cement consumption while preserving strength. HG reports equivalent 28-day compressive strength with 20% less cement in tests.

🚗 PLASTICS — Reduce component weight and material use. HG reports 30% lightweighting in customer programmes.

⚙️ LUBRICANTS — Reduce friction and protect moving parts. HG reports 70% less wear in engine-oil testing.

❄️ AI COOLING — Improve heat transfer through graphene-enhanced cooling fluids and thermal interface materials.

The attraction is the economics. Less material. Less maintenance. Longer service life. Better performance from products manufacturers already sell.

Now imagine just ONE major tyre manufacturer qualifying HydroGraph’s graphene for widespread use.

An illustrative 1 gram per tyre across 100 million tyres would require 100 tonnes of graphene every year. Actual dosage and adoption would depend on qualification. The market is huge: worldwide, around 2.6 billion tyres were produced in 2025.

A tiny ingredient can become substantial recurring demand when it goes into millions of products.

HydroGraph’s October update says multiple advanced customers have progressed into negotiations covering prices, volumes and supply terms. The first larger purchase orders are expected within 2026.
